territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons making tools available in interstate commerce and to covered platforms available to users in the United States.

evidence.quote: available to users in the United States

summary.short: Would require providers of tools creating synthetic or covered content to let users attach provenance information from two years after enactment; bar removing it deceptively or by covered platforms; bar unconsented AI training or generation with marked covered content; enforced by FTC, attorneys general and private suits.
summary.long: As introduced in the Senate (S. 1396, 9 April 2025), the bill would require persons who, for a commercial purpose, make available in interstate commerce a tool primarily used to create synthetic or covered content to let users include content provenance information, from two years after enactment, with security measures to keep it machine-readable and not easily removed. Knowingly removing or tampering with provenance information in an unfair or deceptive practice is unlawful, as is removal by covered platforms (with a security-research exception). Knowingly using covered content bearing provenance information to train AI or generate synthetic content is unlawful without express, informed consent and compliance with usage terms. The Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology would facilitate standards and detection research and a public education campaign within one year. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations; state attorneys general and content owners may sue, with a four-year limitation period for private actions.

relations.target_text: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (15 U.S.C. 9401), section 5002
relations.note: Sec. 3(1) defines 'artificial intelligence' by reference to section 5002 of that Act. The bill does not otherwise amend, implement or cite it.

relations.target_text: Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.), including section 18(a)(1)(B) (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B))
relations.note: Sec. 7(a)(1) treats a violation of the Act as a violation of an FTC rule under section 18(a)(1)(B). Sec. 7(a)(2)(A)-(B) applies the FTC Act's enforcement powers, jurisdiction, penalties and privileges. Sec. 7(a)(2)(C) preserves other Commission authority.

evidence.quote: of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B))

relations.note: Sec. 3(5) defines 'covered content' by reference to works of authorship described in section 102 of title 17.
Sec. 7(b)(5)(A)(i) sets venue for state attorney general civil actions by reference to the venue rules in section 1391 of title 28.

notes: Introduced Senate text (IS) of 9 April 2025, referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Relations are cross-references only: no legal basis, amendment, repeal or implementation is stated. Internal points: Sec. 3(8) defines 'Director' as the USPTO head, and Sec. 4(b) and Sec. 5(b) consult the Register of Copyrights, which the text does not define. Sec. 1 refers to a table of contents that is not in the text. Sec. 9 refers to 'an amendment made by this Act', but the bill makes none. Sec. 6(c) refers to violation of 'subsection (b)' without specifying paragraph (1) or (2).

thresholds.conditions: Alternative to the monthly active users test in Sec. 3(6)(B) ('either'); the service must also be available to users in the United States.
